result.title: Loss-Invariant Projections as Passive Probes of Learned Representations
result.summary: Learned feature representations in neural networks often contain structure beyond that directly used by the final task output. We study this structure using $\textit{passive probes}$ that apply fixed, untrained, property-independent projections to representations as they evolve during training. We motivate this approach through the task of prediction on $S^2$ where equivalent vector and Hermitian parameterizations reveal an additional loss-invariant trace coordinate. This motivates a general construction in which fixed random projections serve as observers of learned features. Because the observer is loss-invariant and independent of the property being studied, changes in accessibility reflect changes in the representation relative to the fixed observer rather than adaptation of the observer itself. We show that ensembles of passive probes can directly reflect task-relevant information such as target alignment. Under our constructions, the accessibility of eventual difficulty evolves differently across tasks. It increases during training in the regression tasks of surface-normal estimation and image inpainting but remains near its initial level in image classification. Comparisons with learned linear probes further show that recoverability and passive accessibility can evolve differently during training. Together, these results show how passive probes can separately characterize changes in representation geometry and the accessibility of eventual task difficulty.

AI.brief_summary: 提出「被动探针」：在训练过程中用固定、未训练且与属性无关的随机投影观察表征，并用 S² 预测中向量与 Hermitian 参数化发现的 loss-invariant trace 坐标来动机化该构造，追踪任务相关信息的可及性变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其固定观测器分离「表征几何变化」与「属性可恢复性」的思路，可能为诊断 VLM 内部视觉证据是否真正被读取、以及 latent 相似度中内容与深度/位置因素提供可核查的探针设计线索。
